technical_data.email_spoofing_technique: The attacker registered a homograph domain 'dropb0x-cloud.com' replacing the letter 'o' with zero and embedded base64 encoded Dropbox logo image to appear legitimate. SPF passed due to configured DNS records, but DKIM and DMARC failed causing quarantine.

Received: from mail.dropb0x-cloud.com (mail.dropb0x-cloud.com [203.0.113.77]) by mx.yourcompany.com with ESMTPS

indicators: Email SPF pass but DKIM and DMARC fail
Sender IP 203.0.113.77 not associated with legitimate Dropbox services
Phishing URL resembles official Dropbox verification page
Phishing page mimics Dropbox login form
Base64 embedded image matching Dropbox logo
SMTP logs showing direct submission from suspicious mail server
samples.detection_method: Employ email authentication checks verifying SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment. Use machine learning to detect homograph domains and inspect embedded image content. Conduct sandbox analysis of URLs and monitor network logs for POSTs to suspicious domains. Educate users with simulated phishing exercises. Network proxies and EDR tools to detect credential submission patterns.

technical_data.email_spoofing_technique: The attacker used a typosquatting domain 'paypa1-secure.com' replacing the letter 'l' with digit '1'. SPF records are misconfigured leading to neutral results, DKIM fails, and DMARC fails without enforcement. Embedded JavaScript captures credentials silently and exfiltrates to a remote server.

Received: from mail.paypa1-secure.com (mail.paypa1-secure.com [192.0.2.99]) by mx.yourcompany.com with ESMTPS

indicators: SPF neutral, DKIM fail, DMARC fail without quarantine or reject
Sender IP 192.0.2.99 not owned by PayPal
Embedded JavaScript in email body capturing credentials
Phishing URL closely mimics official PayPal login page
SMTP logs show direct mail submission from suspicious IP
User agents indicate normal browsers but unusual crawling activity
samples.detection_method: Combine email authentication checks with heuristics to identify typosquatting domains. Use sandboxing to detect embedded malicious scripts. Monitor network traffic for unusual POST requests to unknown domains. User training to recognize unexpected login requests. Utilize EDR and proxy logs to detect credential exfiltration attempts.
